review.why: Fix text that sounds machine-written: detect the tells, vary rhythm, add specifics and inject a brand voice, with a local scoring script.
review.summary: Three modes: detect AI patterns by severity, remove them (filler words, hedging, uniform paragraphs, vague claims), then inject the brand's voice from one example. A local script scores human-ness from 0 to 100, and two references hold an AI-tells checklist and voice techniques.
strengths: Replaces instead of deleting: each flagged phrase comes with better alternatives and a before and after example.
Knows its limits: a piece with too many tells needs a rewrite, and it will not invent specific data.
Asks for one example of the right voice instead of guessing a voice.
cautions: The vocabulary is English-centered and ages fast: the checklist says it was validated in 2026-06 and that newer models show different tells.
The score is a heuristic and does not show who wrote a text.
SKILL.md read in full; the scorer's first 90 lines were read and the rest searched for network and shell calls (none found); the two references were skimmed; not run here.
